# Video script: Which contracts when

> DRAFT - NOT FOR CLINICAL USE. Contains claims with status 'ai-extracted' that no clinician has verified.

Unit F2 | Target length: 7 min

| # | Shot | Narration | Claims |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Presenter with a simple ladder diagram | To name a rhythm, you need to know when the atria contract, when the ventricles contract, and how the two are linked. | - |
| 2 | M-mode trace, atrial and ventricular walls labelled | M-mode. One line through an atrial wall and a ventricular free wall. Both movements on one trace. | AS23-017 |
| 3 | Doppler trace of superior vena cava and aorta, A and V marked | Or pulsed-wave Doppler across two flows together, such as the superior vena cava and the ascending aorta, so atrial and ventricular events appear on one trace. | AS23-018 |
| 4 | Animated ladder diagram: premature atrial beat, then premature ventricular beat | A premature atrial beat resets the atrial rhythm. A premature ventricular beat leaves the atrial rhythm undisturbed. | AS23-074, AS23-075 |
| 5 | Animated ladder diagrams of flutter and complete block | Flutter: fast sawtooth atria, and only some beats get through. Complete block: atria and ventricles each keep their own time, the ventricles slow. | AS23-080, AS23-083 |
| 6 | Animated ladder diagram of blocked atrial bigeminy beside complete block | And the trap. Blocked early atrial beats can look like heart block. They must be told apart. | AS23-084 |
